The Demand Credit part is right (Appendix C, p.26). The Capacity Reservation Fee part is not: Appendix B's formula is Reservation Fee = Reservation Demand Rate x (Anticipated Demand - max(2.5 MVA, Available Capacity)), so the fee falls on the Anticipated Demand above the greater of 2.5 MVA and the Available Capacity, not simply on 'the reserved demand above 2.5 MVA'. In the text layer the formula's letters are math-italic glyphs (each run repeats its first letter), but the run lengths of the max's second term, 18 and 16, match 'Available Capacity', which Appendix A uses in the same max(2.5 MVA, ...) expression and defines as 'existing usable capacity available on the relevant system component prior to the upgrade'.
verdicts.corrected_value: no minimum bill in the policy; the refund of Eligible Dollars through annual Demand Credits over 120 months is full only when average annual billed demand is at least 90 percent of Anticipated Demand, otherwise prorated; a monthly Capacity Reservation Fee, where it applies, equals the Reservation Demand Rate (70 percent of the Demand Charge in the applicable large load rate schedule, or in the applicable transmission rate schedule at transmission voltage) times Anticipated Demand less the greater of 2.5 MVA and Available Capacity
verdicts.words: 'Reservation Fee = Reservation Demand Rate * (Anticipated Demand - max(2.5 MVA, Available Capacity)' (p.25, printed in math-italic glyphs); 'Available Capacity = existing usable capacity available on the relevant system component prior to the upgrade' (p.24)
